findings.claim: On 29 January 2026 Panama's Supreme Court ruled unconstitutional the concession under which CK Hutchison's Panama Ports Company ran the Balboa and Cristobal terminals, a ruling on the contract, not a finding of wrongdoing by the company. It followed a comptroller audit alleging unpaid sums and irregularities in the 2021 extension, which the company denied; it said the ruling lacked legal basis.

After the ruling Panama took over the two terminals and handed temporary concessions to APM Terminals and an MSC unit. By March 2026 Panama Ports Company had raised its ICC arbitration claim against Panama to over $2 billion; Panama's president rejected its accusations, and the case is pending.

In March 2025 China's market regulator said it would conduct an antitrust review of CK Hutchison's planned sale of its ports business, including the Panama terminals, to a BlackRock-led group, after pro-Beijing commentaries reposted by a central government office called the deal a betrayal. No decision on the review was found; Reuters said in March 2026 the sale was still under discussion.

Hutchison Whampoa held 40.2% of oil producer Husky Energy when Cenovus agreed in October 2020 to buy it in an all-stock deal. In a June 2023 SEC filing, CK Hutchison entities reported holding 16.7% of Cenovus common shares.

Li Ka-shing has given away more than HK$30 billion through the Li Ka Shing Foundation, which he set up in 1980, The Standard reported in December 2024 when Forbes Asia named him a Hero of Philanthropy. Gifts in 2024 included US$15 million to Stanford University.

ecology.reason: Fossil-fuel exposure through a holding, not operations: in a June 2023 SEC filing CK Hutchison entities reported holding 16.7% of oil producer Cenovus, received when Cenovus bought Husky Energy, then 40.2% held by Hutchison Whampoa. Oil is a minority stake, not the core business. No environmental incident or group emissions data was checked.

legal.reason: In January 2026 Panama's Supreme Court ruled unconstitutional the concession under which CK Hutchison's Panama Ports Company ran two canal terminals. It is a constitutional ruling on the contract, not a finding of wrongdoing by the company. The comptroller's audit allegations of unpaid sums remain allegations, denied by the company. No personal liability found.

unresolved.reason: Company-level matters are pending: Panama Ports Company's ICC arbitration claim of over $2 billion against Panama, and China's antitrust review, announced in March 2025, of CK Hutchison's planned sale of its ports business to a BlackRock-led group. No outcome of either was found. No personal matter found.

proposal.counterweights: Li Ka-shing has given away more than HK$30 billion through the Li Ka Shing Foundation, set up in 1980, The Standard reported in December 2024.
proposal.rationale: Legal 0 to 2: the Panama Supreme Court's 2026 ruling against the subsidiary's concession is a major company-level court outcome; level 2 lists a court finding and does not require wrongdoing, which this ruling did not establish. Unresolved 0 to 2: a pending $2bn+ arbitration and a Chinese antitrust review, both company level. Ecology 3 unchanged, now documented by the Cenovus stake; not 4, since oil is not the core business. Politics and social not addressed: Beijing's pressure over the sale does not show proximity or donations.
